decision.title: Collections in the sxml command: directories, their parameters, --collection (packet cli-3)

body.p: , after , , , , . F&O 4.0, 17.1.3 and 17.1.4 leave what a collection URI names to the implementation; the CLI's resolver (apps/sxml/query_collection.c, public API only) makes it a local directory. Rules in docs/CLI.md, "Collections"; glossary directory_collection.

item.p: URI: a file: URI after resolution against the static base URI (a relative one is relative to the working directory, a stylesheet or a module), with parameters after "?" separated by ";" or "&" (as Saxon writes them): select=PATTERN (the file name; "*" any characters, "?" one; default *.xml), recurse=yes|no (default no), on-error=fail|ignore (default fail). Another parameter, a fragment, another scheme or a path that is not a directory: FODC0002 with that reason. No percent-decoding, as the CLI's fn:doc maps file URIs to paths today.

fn:uri-collection: the xs:anyURI of each selected file, the directory's normalized URI (ending "/") plus the relative path, sorted by that path in byte order (code point order; a heap sort, no recursion). Nothing is read; a name that is not UTF-8 is left out.

fn:collection: the document node of each of those files, parsed with sxml_processor_parse_document and the processor's entity resolver, as fn:doc parses a file; document URI and base URI are the file's URI. A file that cannot be read or is not well-formed makes the collection unavailable, FODC0002 with "FILE:LINE:COLUMN: message" (FILE relative to the working directory), or with on-error=ignore is left out. A limit or out of memory stops the evaluation (exit 4). Only XML documents: F&O allows any items, but guessing a format from a file name would break ; JSON, text and binary files are reached through uri-collection and json-doc, unparsed-text or unparsed-binary.

Default collection (XPath 4.0, 2.2.2): --collection=DIR[?PARAMETERS] on xpath, xquery and transform, DIR relative to the working directory. A DIR that is not a directory exits 3 at start; an unknown parameter is a usage error (exit 2). Without it, FODC0002 "There is no default collection; give --collection" (as before, ).

Trust: no flag. Collections read what fn:doc may read (any local file, never the network); listing a directory reveals less than reading its files does. --allow-file-access stays the grant of the EXPath File functions, which also write (). Listing uses the invocation's file system (describe, list, canonicalize; never a write) whether or not that flag is given; where there is none (Windows, ) every collection raises FODC0002.
Recursion: subdirectories are a work list; a directory whose canonical path was listed already (a symbolic link back up) is listed once.

Library, no header change: the loader copies the resolver's NONE description into the FODC0002 of fn:collection (it said "No such collection" for every reason); and a collection document whose document URI fn:doc loaded first is replaced by that node, so doc(u) is collection(d)[i] holds in both orders (17.1.3; kept collection documents only when fn:doc had not loaded the URI).
Not done: xsl:strip-space and other document preparation are not applied to collection documents the host builds (the loader prepares only what it parses); percent-encoded file URIs (fn:doc's, too).

Counts (debug drivers, before and after, these sets only): XQ40 fn-collection 32 passed, fn-uri-collection 7, fn-doc 74, fn-doc-available 43; XP40 25, 7, 68, 43; XT40 collection 5, document 95, merge 115, iterate 51, stream-available 6 — all unchanged. CLI: 15 new or changed end-to-end tests, 253 cli tests pass (debug preset); clang-tidy clean, no call cycle.
